newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended down across the board on Friday with turnover falling to 5.30 million lots from 14.45 million due to dull trading before the weekend, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract dived to 4.35 percent from 17.00 percent on Thursday and the seven-day contract fell to 9.58 percent from 13.50 percent.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Trading was dull due to the weekend, depressing the rates," said one trader. "But with a new domestic A share issue next Tuesday, the rates are likely to go up on Monday."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on a technical rebound after falls in the past few days supported by a rising domestic A share market, traders said.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market dropped to 3.62 million lots from 6.80 million.
The new three-year bond that matures in August 1999 closed up at 105.52 yuan from 105.28 yuan and the most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 122.71 yuan from 122.20.
"The rates had fallen for a few days on institutional profit-taking," said a trader. "Some investors today built positions at low prices." - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
